[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-RTCON-2.7.14.md#abb-context]

### ABB Context

- **Parent L2 Capability**: Container & Image Security — [GUID-SEC-APP-CAP-DESC-1.7.02](../GUID-SEC-APP-CAP-DESC-1.7.02.md)
- **ABB Catalog**: [GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-CAT-2.7.06](../GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-CAT-2.7.06.md)
- **Capability Statement**: The enterprise SHALL have an architectural capability to enforce behavioral constraints on running container processes and detect anomalous container runtime activity that deviates from expected execution profiles.
page_texts.4:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-RTCON-2.7.14.md#abb-scope]

### ABB Scope

**In Scope**:
- Architectural capability to define and enforce allowed process behaviors for running containers (syscall profiles, file system access, network egress)
- Detection of container runtime anomalies such as unexpected process spawning, privilege escalation attempts, or unexpected network connections
- Immutability enforcement — preventing modification of container file systems at runtime

**Out of Scope**:
- Pre-deployment image vulnerability scanning (see GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-IMGSC-2.7.13)
- Orchestration-layer RBAC and workload scheduling policy (see GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-K8SRBAC-2.7.15)
- Host OS security (see Cloud & Infrastructure Security domain)
- Security controls, tool selection, or configuration baselines (`standards/security/`)

[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-RTCON-2.7.14.md#core-principles]

### Core Principles

- Containers SHALL be run with the minimum set of capabilities required for their declared function; all unused OS capabilities SHALL be dropped.
- Container file systems SHOULD be run as read-only where the application design permits, to prevent in-place modification by an attacker.
- Runtime behavioral profiles SHOULD be defined for production workloads; deviations SHALL be alerted to security operations.
- Containers SHALL NOT run as root unless a documented architectural exception has been approved.
page_texts.8:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-RTCON-2.7.14.md#capability-and-profile-enforcement]

#### Capability and Profile Enforcement

**Architectural intent**: Constrain what a container process is permitted to do at the OS level, reducing the blast radius of a compromised container.

**Design guidance**:
- Containers SHALL define a syscall allowlist or seccomp profile appropriate to their workload type.
- Privilege escalation SHALL be prevented at the container runtime configuration level.
- Containers SHOULD declare their required Linux capabilities explicitly; undeclared capabilities SHALL NOT be granted by default.
page_texts.9:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-RTCON-2.7.14.md#anomaly-detection]

#### Anomaly Detection

**Architectural intent**: Identify in-progress exploitation or post-compromise activity within running containers.

**Design guidance**:
- Runtime telemetry SHALL be collected and forwarded to the security monitoring capability (SecOps domain).
- Alerting SHOULD be configured for behaviors that deviate from the established baseline for each workload type.

[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-RTCON-2.7.14.md#integration-interfaces]

### Integration Interfaces

| Interface | Direction | Consuming ABB | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| Workload Deployment | Inbound | GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-K8SRBAC-2.7.15 | Container workload specification including security context |
| Runtime Events | Outbound | SecOps SIEM/Monitoring | Syscall and process events forwarded for detection |
| Policy Enforcement | Bidirectional | Container Runtime | Syscall filter and capability enforcement at process level |

[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-RTCON-2.7.14.md#zero-trust-alignment-nist-sp-800-207]

### Zero Trust Alignment (NIST SP 800-207)

Runtime Container Security advances the Applications and Workloads pillar by enforcing that even admitted, scanned workloads operate within strictly defined behavioral boundaries — operationalizing the assumption that a workload may be compromised and its blast radius must be limited.
page_texts.12:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-RTCON-2.7.14.md#nist-sp-800-53-intent-alignment]

### NIST SP 800-53 Intent Alignment

This ABB enables the architectural intent of the SC (System and Communications Protection) family — specifically process isolation and least-privilege execution — and the SI family, which addresses malicious code protection and system monitoring.
page_texts.13:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-RTCON-2.7.14.md#constraints-and-dependencies]

### Constraints and Dependencies

- Behavioral profile definition requires characterization of expected workload behavior; this is an operational activity that must be part of workload onboarding.
- Overly restrictive profiles can cause application failures; profile testing in pre-production is required before enforcement in production.
- Anomaly detection output must be routed to the SecOps domain; this ABB does not include detection and response capability.
